quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Dr Catherine Suarez is identified in the edition brochure as Coordinator of the DAS; her official faculty profile confirms continuing-education DAS/MAS coordination. She is the strongest first contact to establish learner/speaker travel needs and the accommodation decision pathway. Ms Biata Lysenko is named Administrative Assistant of the DAS in the same edition brochure; she is relevant for practical enquiries and routing, not a proven hotel buyer. Prof François Curtin is programme co-director and a coordination-team member, suitable for academic escalation. None is shown to control hotel contracts.
findings.futureEdition: The 2026–2027 DAS began on 21 September 2026 and its last published teaching dates are 10–11 May 2027. In-horizon activity: Clinical Trial Planning and Set-Up, 18–20 January 2027; Clinical Trial Conduct and Close-Out, 8–10 February; Audits and Inspections, 8–10 March; optional Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls, 19–20 April; Medical Devices, 10–11 May. These are intermittent teaching blocks, not a continuous January–May residential event. No later DAS edition with exact activity dates was located. The main DAS page separately announces the related MAS next edition as 2027–2028, without exact dates; that is not a dated future DAS booking opportunity.
findings.hotelProductFit: Assessment/inference using the supplied hotel brief and published course locations: weak for core housing because teaching is in Geneva city and YOTEL is in Founex. Conditional fit only for nonlocal learners/speakers who accept the commute and whose accommodation is not centrally committed. Short, separated teaching blocks could support ancillary stays, but no actual travelling cohort, attendance or room demand is published. Do not underwrite a 20–120-room block, the 237-room house, or continuous January–May stays. The hotel’s meeting rooms are not a replacement opportunity while the course publishes Geneva teaching locations; a separate future workshop would require an explicit brief. Resort-style retreat demand and banquet scale are not established.
findings.venueCommitments: The edition-specific official brochure publishes two course locations: Fondation Louis Jeantet, 77 route de Florissant, 1208 Geneva; CMU (Centre Médical Universitaire), 1 rue Michel-Servet, 1206 Geneva. Both are in Geneva city, Canton of Geneva, Switzerland—not Founex/Nyon/La Côte/Geneva Airport corridor. No allocation of individual modules to either location or exact classroom is published. These are published teaching locations, not evidence of a signed venue contract or a lodging commitment. No Lausanne or French-border activity is identified; no programme-specific airport-arrival or La Côte lodging evidence was found.
findings.historicalRotation: The programme’s own announcement verifies a 2024–2025 DAS cohort, but supplies no teaching dates or venue. An official standalone Module 7 page still lists 19–21 January 2026 in Geneva, despite being linked from the 2026–2027 programme. Treat it as historical, not a replacement for 18–20 January 2027. Swiss Biotech retains 22 September 2025–12 May 2026 alongside conflicting current-edition metadata. This corroborates earlier activity only weakly; it does not establish historical hotel use or destination rotation. No evidence of a rotating destination or hotel series was found; annual DAS recurrence is not proven.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown. The edition brochure’s relevant practical section says “Course Locations” and names Fondation Louis Jeantet and CMU; its contact is “das-mas-clinical@unige.ch”. Neither the official programme nor brochure publishes a housing bureau, host hotel, hotel list, room block, lodging inclusion, hotel RFP or accommodation booking instructions. Hotels listed for this edition: none found. Silence does not establish that lodging is independently booked or sourcing is open.
findings.organizationStructure: University-owned continuing education, not an association-owned congress, corporate event or agency product. CCDE is the publishing continuing-education centre; the programme’s directors and coordination team are University of Geneva Faculty of Medicine/Faculty of Science personnel as identified on the official programme. No appointed PCO, DMC or external housing agent is disclosed. Accreditation and industry promotion do not make those bodies the event owner or hotel buyer.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The two published course locations are not identified as competing hotels. No incumbent hotel, sold-out condition, overflow arrangement or displacement opportunity is evidenced. Inference: hotels closer to the Geneva teaching sites have a location advantage over Founex; no specific hotel win/loss claim is supported. Published “limited spots available” concerns course registration, not bedrooms.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Dr Catherine Suarez through the published programme office, das-mas-clinical@unige.ch, +41 (0)22 379 54 58; copy/route to Ms Biata Lysenko by name through that office. Ask whether the January–May modules generate nonlocal overnight stays, how many rooms and nights per block, who books/pays, whether any accommodation agreement already exists, and which module uses which venue. Only if sourcing is free and a Founex commute is acceptable, offer a small demand-led ancillary rate proposal; otherwise retain a low-priority future relationship. Do not reserve inventory or claim a group block before an actual brief.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: The current programme is underway as of 17 November 2026, but five teaching blocks remain within the requested horizon. Individual modules can be registered for up to four weeks before the module starts, subject to places. This is course accessibility, not hotel procurement accessibility. Lodging may already be arranged, centrally contracted or unnecessary for local participants; none is resolved publicly. Do not pitch relocation of the scheduled teaching.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference/strategy: cultivate the programme office for permission-based accommodation referrals or a future ancillary workshop only after nonlocal demand and sourcing freedom are confirmed. Repeated DAS activity supports a relationship-development hypothesis, not guaranteed annual dates. The related MAS 2027–2028 mention is a monitoring lead only; no exact dates, open hotel requirement or move toward La Côte is evidenced.
